title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-03-01
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
source: Recording Info: SBD Master Reels -> Dat (Panasonic 3700); Transfer Info: Delta DiO 2496 sound card > HD > CD-R; Mastering Info: HD > CD WAV > Cool Edit > Trader's Little Helper 2.7 > xACT 2.35 FLAC 8; Mastering by Seth Kaplan (alligator69@optonline.net) March 25, 2015

ai_review.summary: Great‑sounding soundboard capture with solid performance highlights like Cumberland Blues and The Big Boy Pete, though the show runs a bit mellow.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as clear and outstanding despite brief cuts, making it one of the better sources for this era. Musically the night is described as okay overall – standout moments include a blazing "Big Boy Pete," superb "Cumberland Blues" and a tight "King Bee," while the down‑tempo take on "Uncle John’s Band" and feedback‑laden "The Other One" feel less inspired.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong recording quality (high marks) balanced against an average‑to‑good performance with both highlights and slower, less engaging moments.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall great sound; brief cuts are unobtrusive. Some feedback on "The Other One" forced the band to lower volume, but the mix remains clear and balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set leans toward a mellow, down‑tempo vibe after early feedback problems; highlights are interspersed with slower, less energetic numbers.
